content.content:
- F-289 **The distance's zero holds under the bound `Any`, which the compile command does not set yet: under its setting the twelve give 685 errors, 580 of them on the bound `Object`.** The distance stage turns the extends-`Object` pre-desugaring off, as walk does; `fortress compile` still sets it (`Shell.useCompilerLibraries()`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/Shell.java:371-372`; row 412). The stage under the compile setting, `run.sh … compile`, gives `#total 685` (`bound-Object 580`, `typecheck 105`, `#crash none`), measured once on climb batch 22's code; no test checks it. So the zero (F-53) reaches the switch-over only once the compiled path ends that departure, as P-42 requires (row 412). Under the bound `Any`, the compiled tests that import `CompilerSystem` pass, and the compiled tracks fail only on test-side costs (F-292). Detail: `reviews/phase3-exit/zero-audit.md`, "A.3 The settings, and what the tools leave out".

- F-291 **With the bound `Any`, the compiled path compiles, loads and runs generics at tuple and arrow static arguments as it does with `extends Any` written; `()` fails whatever the bound (row 339), and so does a generic dotted method with one tuple-typed parameter (row 832).** Measured once, with row 412's switch (`Shell.java:372`) turned off by a patch that did not land: generic functions, objects and traits, dispatch to a generic arm and `typecase`, at a pair or an arrow, with the static argument written or inferred. The class loader made the same classes by name, and the program jars read the same under `javap`, as the same programs with `extends Any` written under the compile command's bound `Object`. So the switch to the bound `Any` costs the run time no work for these shapes; its test cost is F-292. Not run: the one library's own instantiations at tuples, tuples of three or more and nested ones, generic functional methods at a tuple, a native that receives a tuple. Under the compile command's bound `Object`, they are refused (row 412), pass unchecked where the static argument is written (row 470), or, for `q = id((3, 4))`, run `id(3)` (row 691). No gated test. Detail: `perf-probes/bound-any-compiled/REPORT.md`, "The shapes by setting" and "What the class loader makes".

- F-292 **With the bound `Any`, the compiled test tracks give 12 failures in 10 tests of `CompilerJUTest`, every one a cost on the test side, and none in the library and othercompiler tracks; the 23 `.test` files of the compiled tests that import `CompilerSystem` pass under either bound.** Measured once, with row 412's switch off by a patch that did not land, on code equal to climb batch 22's gate, which passed all three tracks: `ant testQuick` gave compiler 1315 tests, 12 failures; library 86, 0; othercompiler 263, 0. The 12, by kind: 1, the promotion of `XXXImplicitBoundAny` that row 412's fix owes; 3, pinned diagnostics that print the bound; 4, `comprises` tests that write `where [\E extends Object\]` as a workaround of row 412; 1, `XXXOverrideGenericReturnTypeNotSubtype`, whose premise rests on the bound `Object` (row 653); and 3, the compile, link and run of `CoercionGenericFnCompiledRungC`, which meets the compiler prelude's `String` `||` at `Object` until the switch-over. So the switch is the one line and ten test edits. The 23 files gave `OK (138 tests)` under both bounds. Not run under the bound `Any`: the rest of the gate and the count stage (F-289). Detail: `perf-probes/bound-any-compiled/REPORT.md`, "The CompilerSystem tests, and the compiled tracks, under (ii) against (i)".

- F-38 **The compiled dispatcher chooses an overload arm generic in a size by the value's size, and the arm reads its size.** Called with an argument typed `Any`, the dispatcher reads the size off the value's descriptor. The checker's return-type rule compares the arms' own sizes (row 410). The dispatcher skips the bound `Object` that the compile path gives a size parameter (row 412). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatRtDisp`, `NatRtDispSize` and `NatRtDispTrait`. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/size-probes.md` section 2.

- F-55 **Static arguments are inferred with coercion on both paths: the compiled checker from the arguments' static types and the expected type, walk from their run-time types.** So a mixed-width call takes the narrowest type into which its arguments convert, as P-74 decides. F-73 gives the checker's rule and F-137 walk's; F-87 lists where the checker has an expected type. Under walk, a typed binding converts a call's result after the call and does not fix the call's static arguments: `a: BoxK[\ZZ64\] = wrapK(3)` infers `T` from `3` as `Int` and is refused, since no coercion converts a `BoxK[\Int\]` (row 510). On the compile path, a parameter with no written bound is bounded by `Object`, not `Any` (row 412), so a parameter that nothing fixes takes `Object` there (F-78). Gated by `compiler_tests/InferCoercionShapes` and `tests/InferCoercionRungK`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-inference-checker/REPORT.md` section 3.2; `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 9.

- F-129 **A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`, and a program whose sizes are known at compile time loads, dispatches and runs compiled, apart from the open cases below.** It builds P-41. Each size value, such as the 3 of `Vec[\3\]`, has one descriptor; in a run-time subtype test, it is a supertype only of an equal size. A size read as a value is a constant that the class loader replaces by the numeral. Closures and tasks capture a size as a free static parameter (F-135). A size made from a number known only at run time does not run compiled: `tests/NatReflectTest.fss` stops at load (row 307). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatRt*`. Also open on the compiled path: a `ZZ32Vector` passed to a generic constructor fails at load (row 408); the compiled path gives every static parameter with no `extends` clause, a size among them, the bound `Object`, not the specification's `Any` (row 412); a dispatched overload arm whose static parameter has a concrete generic bound stops the compile in its sized form and dies at load in its type form (row 413); an object that extends two instantiations of one trait, one at a static parameter, passes the checker and dies at load (row 414). Row 416 is walk's defect: walk refuses at load `g(b: Tg[\3\])` beside `g(b: Tg[\4\])`, which the compiled run dispatches, since walk's overloading check applies no exclusion of instantiations. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-size-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 9.

- F-173 **The specification's type-inference chapter states the rule that the compiled checker builds: the declaration is chosen first, then its static arguments are inferred.** It states P-46, P-48 and P-49. A type parameter that a parameter's declared type mentions inside another type, as `List[\T\]` mentions `T`, is fixed by the argument at that position. One that is the whole declared type of one or more parameters, as `T` is of `x: T`, and that nothing else fixes, takes the narrowest type, within its bounds, that every one of those arguments has or converts into: `ZZ64` for a `ZZ32` and an `NN32`. Where there is none, and no numeral settles the tie, it takes its bound, narrowed by what the call's expected type requires of the return type (P-48). So does a type parameter that neither an argument nor the expected type fixes. Inference never gives a type parameter `BottomType`. The compiled path departs from the chapter in these ways, among others. It bounds a type parameter written without an `extends` clause by `Object`, not `Any`, as the chapter's callouts say (row 412, P-42). Its prelude lacks the coercion of `NN32` into `ZZ64`, so a `ZZ32` and an `NN32` instantiate a type parameter at `ZZ`, not `ZZ64`; no callout names this (row 442, `compiler_tests/XXXInferPromoteNN32`). The callouts at `Specification/basic/inference.tex:236-298` and `:364-425` also give walk's departures, such as the return type `BottomType` that walk gives a function expression that declares none (row 587). Plain tests gate the rule for a type parameter that is a parameter's whole type, at its bound where no argument type is narrowest, on both paths: `compiler_tests/InferLone*` and `tests/InferLone*Walk.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/REPORT.md` (the bound rule); `Specification/basic/inference.tex:47-124` (the chapter's rule).

- F-274 **Under walk, two declarations whose declared domains are equal are refused by the No Duplicates Rule, where one has static parameters of its own and the other has its own or none, whether or not the parameter-by-parameter check orders them.** The parameter check reads a type parameter as strictly below its bound. So it orders `h[\T extends Number\](x: T, y: T)` before `h(x: Number, y: Number)`, though their declared domains are equal. Walk compares the declared domains, each declaration's over all its own instances, and refuses the pair: "fails because their parameter lists have the same types" (F-257). A type parameter bounded by `Any` counts: walk refuses `g[\T\](a: T)` beside `g(a: Any)`, and the compiled checker accepts that pair (row 759). Gated by `tests/GenericBesideGenericSameDomain`, `GenericBesidePlainSameDomain`, `NoDuplicatesRuleWalk` and `NoDuplicatesRuleSizeWalk` (refused). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-generic-pairs/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 5; `compile-ladder/rung-existential-reduction/REPORT.md` section 5 (row 759 on both paths).

\end{description}

\subsection{An abstract method of an exported trait}
\seclabel{revival-export-abstract}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected section] \secref{export-statements}.
\item[Change] The rule by which a trait or object declaration of a component
satisfies an exported one asks, beside a satisfying declaration for each field
declaration and non-abstract method declaration of the exported declaration, a
method declaration for each abstract method declaration of it, with the same
header apart from the modifier \KWD{abstract}, with a body or without one.
The sentence that allows a concrete declaration for an abstract method stands.
The passage gains a box.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
revival's decision of 25~October 2026, which the revival confirmed against this
passage on 29~October 2026, that a method that an \apiN\ declares abstract is
declared in the component that exports the \apiN.
The decision takes the type group's later work over this text, as the revival
does wherever the two conflict.
The compiler's own library declares, in its \apiN, the abstract methods of its
trait \TYP{GeneratorZZ32}, such as \VAR{loop}, and restates each of them in its
component without a body
(\nolinkurl{Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi}, lines 110--120, and
\nolinkurl{Library/CompilerLibrary.fss}, lines 301--312, in the revival's
repository).
The team's compiled type checker compared every member of an exported trait
with the component's: in 2009 member by member, an abstract method matched
by a declaration of the same header apart from the modifier \KWD{abstract}
(Sukyoung Ryu, commit \texttt{edb516dba}), and in its snapshots of 2011 and
2012 by refusing a component whose trait has fewer members than the
exported one (commit \texttt{5a68404fd}, the last).
The code generator makes a call of a method through a trait an interface call
on the component's declaration of the trait, so a compiled call of an abstract
method that the component's trait leaves out, or declares at another header,
stops at run time with \texttt{NoSuchMethodError}, also where every object
defines the method (row~816 of the revival's gap ledger).
\Library\ followed the earlier practice of the interpreter, which finds a
method on the object by name at a call and never needed the declaration, and
left twelve such methods undeclared in their component
\TYP{FortressLibrary}; the component now declares them, without bodies.
The text of \secref{apis}, which asks a matching definition to include
definitions for all declarations other than the methods and fields declared
abstract, is unchanged: it asks no body for an abstract method, and the revised
rule asks none either.
A reversal would restore the original sentences and return the compiled
export check to asking no declaration for an abstract method of an exported
trait, so that a compiled call of a method that a component leaves out stops
at run time again; the twelve declarations of \library\ would then be
unnecessary, though harmless, or the code generator would declare such a
method in the component's interface itself, a change that still leaves a
method declared at another header, a narrower return type and a functional
method failing at run time.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-abstract-declared/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
\item[Effect] The compiled type checker refuses a component whose trait leaves
out a method that the exported trait declares abstract (``missing members of
the trait/object in the component'') or declares it at another header
(``different method''), and takes a declaration with a body or without one.
The interpreter compares no component with the \apisN\ it exports, so it loads
and runs a component that leaves such a method out, or declares it at another
header, where each object defines it (row~NEW-A-1 of the revival's gap
ledger).
\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/components/source-code.tex},
lines 380--385, which the change revises:
\begin{quote}
and contains,
for each field declaration and non-abstract method declaration
in the exported declaration,
a satisfying declaration (or a set of declarations).
When a trait has an abstract method declared,
a satisfying trait declaration is allowed to provide a concrete declaration.
\end{quote}
\item[Route C] The same under route~C.
\end{description}

A component must include, for every \apiN\ $A$ it exports,
matching definitions for all the declarations in $A$.
A matching definition of a declaration $d$
is a definition $d'$ with the same name as $d$
that includes definitions for all declarations

The header and type of $d'$ must be the same as the header and type of $d$.
$d'$ may include additional definitions not declared in $d$.

content.content:
- F-282 **The compiled export check matches an api's members by name and header and reads `abstract`, and the `FortressLibrary` component matches its api.** It matches an api member with a component member of the same name and header, a field by its name, its modifiers other than `var` and its type, and an object's value parameter likewise, by its modifiers other than `var` (`compiler_tests/ExportVarObjectParameter`). It compares the component's abstract members against the api's, and asks no definition for an api member written `abstract` (`Specification/basic/components/apis.tex:252-256`). So a component may leave out, or declare at another header, a member its api writes `abstract`, and a client's call of it dies at run time with `NoSuchMethodError` (row 816). `FortressLibrary.fsi` states its component's members at the component's headers. That covers the 66 members written `abstract` (`String`'s nine among them), the follow-on lines, `Array2`'s subscripts, `TotalComparison`'s `=`, `RR64`'s `^`, `Condition` with `ZeroIndexed` and its range subscript, `Maybe`'s header, `Just`'s `SQCAP` and `SQCUP`, `ActualReduction`'s distributes, and `BigReduction`'s and `Comprehension`'s parameters. It leaves out the subscripts the component never built (`Just`'s and `Nothing`'s 1.0 range subscripts, the arrays' `OpenRange` subscripts). Where the api's type is the contract, the component takes it: `RR64`'s brackets and `truncate` at `ZZ64`, `DelegatedIndexed`'s `generator`, and `Array2`'s and `Array3`'s `bounds` and `zeroIndices`. `String`'s api writes `abstract` on the members its component's trait leaves without a body or does not declare, and its `excludes` clause is the component's (F-286). So among the members the export check reads, it finds no difference, and the distance holds no export error; it reads every top-level operator under its declared name (F-287). That zero rests on the reading of `abstract` above, which P-158 replaces: a member that an api writes `abstract` is declared in the component (row 816). Gated by `compiler_tests/XXXExportMemberName`, `XXXExportFieldName`, `ExportVarFieldMatchesField`, `ExportComprisesEllipsisAbstract`, `ExportAbstractMemberDefined` and `ExportAbstractMemberAbsent`, and by the distance stage's per-site list. Walk's values of the moved members are gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/ExportAlignedMembersWalk.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-export-align/REPORT.md` sections 1, 5 and 6; `compile-ladder/rung-export-last/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 2; `compile-ladder/rung-string-members/REPORT.md` section 5.

- F-286 **The api's `String` writes `abstract` on every member that its component's trait leaves without a body or does not declare, and every string object defines them.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2447-2522` writes 14 of `String`'s members `abstract`: `size`, `depth`, `asFlatString`, `isBalanced`, `verify`, `asDebugStringIndented`, `get`, `uncheckedSubstring`, `rangeContains`, `splitWithOffsets`, `split`, `balanced`, `opr ||(self, c:Char)` and `writeOn`. The component's trait (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4336-4446`) declares 7 of them, none with a body, and leaves out `depth`, `isBalanced`, `verify`, `rangeContains`, `balanced`, `splitWithOffsets` and `split`. `FlatString`, `CatString`, `EmptyString` and `SubString` each define all 14 under walk. `String`'s `excludes` clause is `{ Number, Char, AnyMultiplicativeRing }` on both sides; `AnyList` states its exclusion of `String` itself (`Library/List.fsi:55`). So `String` has no entry in the `FortressLibrary` export error (F-282).
